# Vilivity

> A reference for Black health: skin, hair, mind, body and food. Each entry opens with a plain answer, then do, avoid and when to see someone, then the evidence. Every claim has a source and a tier (A tested in people like you, B tested elsewhere or observed in Black populations, C lab only, D untested) with a strength (strong, moderate, thin). Entries are not yet clinically reviewed. This is information, not medical advice.

How we grade: https://vilivity.com/about/evidence/
Machine-readable entries: https://vilivity.com/api/entries/index.json
The Untested List (open research questions, each with the study that would settle it): https://vilivity.com/untested/

## Skin

- [Acne on dark skin](https://vilivity.com/skin/acne-on-dark-skin/): Acne in dark skin often leaves dark marks that last longer than the spots, so treating acne early matters most. Tier B thin.
- [African black soap](https://vilivity.com/skin/black-soap-and-african-black-soap/): Nobody has tested African black soap on acne, eczema or dark marks in people. Tier D.
- [Baby skin care (newborns and infants)](https://vilivity.com/skin/baby-skin-care/): Newborn skin needs very little: plain water baths for the first month, no cleansers or lotions, and leave vernix on. Tier B moderate.
- [Collagen supplements for skin and joints](https://vilivity.com/skin/collagen-supplements/): Collagen supplements may add a little skin moisture in trials, but the best-quality trials and the ones not paid for by the industry found no clear skin effect. Tier B thin.
- [Dark circles under the eyes](https://vilivity.com/skin/dark-circles-under-the-eyes/): Dark circles under the eyes can come from pigment, thin skin showing blood vessels, or lost volume, and the cause decides the treatment. Tier B thin.
- [Dark marks after acne (post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation)](https://vilivity.com/skin/dark-marks-after-acne/): Dark marks after spots are common in dark skin and slow to fade. Tier A thin.
- [Dark or swollen lips](https://vilivity.com/skin/dark-or-swollen-lips/): Dark lips are often a harmless variation in pigment. Tier B thin.
- [Dark velvety patches on the neck and folds (acanthosis nigricans)](https://vilivity.com/skin/acanthosis-nigricans/): Dark, thick, velvety patches in the neck, armpits or groin are called acanthosis nigricans. Tier B thin.
- [Eczema on dark skin (atopic eczema, including babies)](https://vilivity.com/skin/eczema-on-dark-skin/): Eczema on dark skin often looks grey, purple, brown or darker, not red, with very dry, thickened or bumpy skin. Tier B thin.
- [Finding a dermatologist who knows dark skin](https://vilivity.com/skin/finding-a-dermatologist-for-dark-skin/): Dark skin is under-represented in textbooks, and in one test dermatologists and AI both did worse on dark-skin photos, so it is fair to ask a clinician about their experience. Tier B thin.
- [How skin conditions look on dark skin (redness, rashes, rosacea, sunburn)](https://vilivity.com/skin/conditions-look-different-on-dark-skin/): Redness on dark skin can look pink, purple, brown, grey or just a subtle darkening, so it is easy to miss. Tier B thin.
- [Keloids and piercings](https://vilivity.com/skin/keloids-and-piercings/): Keloids run in families and are much more common in people of African ancestry. Tier B moderate.
- [Laser hair removal on dark skin](https://vilivity.com/skin/laser-hair-removal-on-dark-skin/): Laser hair removal can work in medium to dark skin, but the laser also targets skin pigment, so burns and dark or pale marks are more likely. Tier B thin.
- [Melasma](https://vilivity.com/skin/melasma/): Melasma is brown or greyish patches on the face, linked to sun, pregnancy and hormonal medicines. Tier B moderate.
- [Moisturising and 'ashy' skin](https://vilivity.com/skin/moisturising-and-ashy-skin/): Ashiness is dry skin showing as a grey-white look on dark skin. Tier A thin.
- [Shaving and razor bumps (pseudofolliculitis barbae)](https://vilivity.com/skin/shaving-and-razor-bumps/): Razor bumps happen when tightly curled hair grows back into the skin after shaving. Tier A thin.
- [Shea butter](https://vilivity.com/skin/shea-butter/): Shea butter has been used on skin and hair in West Africa for generations, but no controlled trial has tested plain shea butter on skin. Tier D.
- [Skin ageing in dark skin](https://vilivity.com/skin/skin-ageing-in-dark-skin/): Reviews say darker skin tends to show lines and sun damage later, helped by more melanin and a thicker, more compact dermis. Tier B thin.
- [Skin cancer and moles on dark skin](https://vilivity.com/skin/skin-cancer-and-moles-on-dark-skin/): Skin cancer is much rarer in Black people, but it can happen, and when melanoma does, outcomes are worse. Tier B moderate.
- [Skin lightening and bleaching creams](https://vilivity.com/skin/skin-lightening-creams/): Many skin lightening creams contain mercury, strong steroids or high-strength hydroquinone, and reported cases show serious skin and kidney harm. Tier B moderate.
- [Skincare routine basics (and Korean multi-step routines)](https://vilivity.com/skin/skincare-routine-basics/): A short routine is what dermatologist guidance recommends: gentle cleanser, moisturiser and sunscreen. Tier D.
- [Stretch marks and fading scars](https://vilivity.com/skin/stretch-marks-and-scar-fading/): No cream, butter or oil has been shown to stop stretch marks, and a trial of cocoa butter in pregnant women found it made no difference. Tier B moderate.
- [Sunscreen on dark skin](https://vilivity.com/skin/sunscreen-on-dark-skin/): Dark skin burns less easily and melanoma is rarer, but when it happens it is found later and survival is worse. Tier B moderate.
- [Sweat, body odour and deodorant](https://vilivity.com/skin/body-odour-and-sweat/): Sweating and odour are normal. Tier B thin.
- [Vitiligo](https://vilivity.com/skin/vitiligo/): Vitiligo is loss of skin colour in patches, an autoimmune condition, not an infection. Tier B moderate.

## Hair

- [Babies' and children's hair](https://vilivity.com/hair/children-and-babies-hair/): Children's hair is best handled the way adults' is: gently, with hair wet and conditioned for detangling. Tier B moderate.
- [Braids, cornrows and twists for men and boys](https://vilivity.com/hair/mens-and-boys-braids-cornrows-and-twists/): No study has tested braid styles in men or boys. Tier D.
- [Braids, twists and extensions: tension, how long, itch](https://vilivity.com/hair/braids-twists-and-extensions/): Braids that hurt are too tight; pain after installation means pull on the scalp. Tier B moderate.
- [CCCA: scarring hair loss at the crown](https://vilivity.com/hair/central-centrifugal-cicatricial-alopecia/): CCCA is a scarring hair loss that starts as a thin patch at the crown and spreads outwards. Tier B thin.
- [Chebe powder: length retention, growth claims and safety](https://vilivity.com/hair/chebe-powder-and-hair-length/): Chebe is a traditional herbal hair powder, mixed with oil or butter and coated on the lengths. Tier D.
- [Chemical relaxers and hair straighteners](https://vilivity.com/hair/chemical-relaxers/): Studies disagree on whether relaxers raise cancer risk, and none can prove cause. Tier B moderate.
- [Choosing a stylist, braider or loctician](https://vilivity.com/hair/choosing-a-stylist-braider-or-loctician/): No study shows that a stylist's training or specialism gives better hair or scalp outcomes. Tier D.
- [Colouring and bleaching afro-textured hair](https://vilivity.com/hair/colouring-and-bleaching-textured-hair/): Bleaching and dyeing damage the hair surface whatever the curl, in lab tests on hair samples; no study has tested a colour or bleach routine in people with coiled hair. Tier D.
- [Dry, itchy, flaky scalp and dandruff](https://vilivity.com/hair/scalp-itch-dandruff-and-seborrhoeic-dermatitis/): Flaking and itch are often dandruff or seborrhoeic dermatitis, which is a skin reaction, not simple dryness. Tier B moderate.
- [Finding a stylist, trichologist or dermatologist who knows afro hair](https://vilivity.com/hair/finding-a-hair-and-scalp-specialist/): A stylist or loctician is the right person for styling and a trichologist or dermatologist for hair loss. Tier D.
- [Going natural: transitioning from a relaxer and the big chop](https://vilivity.com/hair/transitioning-to-natural-hair-and-the-big-chop/): There is no study of the big chop or of how to grow out a relaxer, so none of this is tested. Tier D.
- [Hair breakage, growth and keeping length](https://vilivity.com/hair/hair-breakage-and-length-retention/): Tightly coiled hair does grow, but it breaks more easily when combed or handled, so the length you keep depends on breakage. Tier D.
- [Hair growth oils and supplements: castor, rosemary, black seed, biotin](https://vilivity.com/hair/hair-growth-oils-and-supplements/): Castor oil alone and black seed oil have not been tested for hair growth in people in my search. Tier D.
- [Hair porosity and moisture](https://vilivity.com/hair/hair-porosity-and-moisture/): The glass-of-water float test, and routines chosen by "low, normal or high porosity", have never been tested in people. Tier D.
- [Hair shedding after pregnancy, illness or stress](https://vilivity.com/hair/hair-shedding-and-thinning-after-pregnancy-or-stress/): A sudden all-over shed, usually three months after a trigger such as childbirth, illness, stress or crash dieting, is called telogen effluvium. Tier D.
- [Hair transplants in afro-textured hair](https://vilivity.com/hair/hair-transplants-in-afro-textured-hair/): Transplants can be done on tightly curled hair, but the evidence is a small case series and a review, with no outcome data in Black men. Tier D.
- [Hair types 4a, 4b, 4c: what typing tells you](https://vilivity.com/hair/hair-texture-types-and-typing/): The 4a, 4b and 4c letters sort curl by eye and were not checked against measured hair. Tier D.
- [Head lice in afro-textured hair and locs](https://vilivity.com/hair/head-lice-in-afro-hair-and-locs/): Anyone with hair can get head lice. Tier B thin.
- [Heat, silk press, keratin treatments and colour](https://vilivity.com/hair/heat-styling-silk-press-and-smoothing-treatments/): Heat damage on afro hair has not been measured in people. Tier B thin.
- [LOC and LCO: layering liquid, oil and cream](https://vilivity.com/hair/moisture-layering-loc-and-lco-methods/): Nobody has tested layering liquid, oil and cream on people, so there is no proof that LOC or LCO beats one product or that either order is better. Tier D.
- [Locs: starting, washing and keeping them healthy](https://vilivity.com/hair/locs-starting-washing-and-maintenance/): No study has tested how often to wash or retwist locs. Tier D.
- [Men's afro hair: waves, fades, durags and the nape](https://vilivity.com/hair/mens-hair-waves-fades-and-durags/): No study has tested a waves routine or durags for scalp or hair health. Tier D.
- [Protecting your edges and hairline](https://vilivity.com/hair/edges-and-hairline/): Edges thin mainly from pulling: tight styles, glue on the hairline and frequent heat are linked to hairline loss. Tier B moderate.
- [Receding hairline and hair transplants in Black men](https://vilivity.com/hair/mens-hair-loss-and-hair-transplants/): Receding hairlines have several causes: inherited pattern baldness, pulling from tight styles, or scarring conditions such as CCCA, which men can get. Tier D.
- [Relaxer, texturiser, perm and keratin: what is the difference](https://vilivity.com/hair/relaxer-texturiser-perm-and-keratin-differences/): A relaxer straightens, a texturiser loosens curl by being left on for less time, and a perm adds curl. Tier D.
- [Scalp oiling and greasing](https://vilivity.com/hair/scalp-oiling-and-greasing/): Nobody has tested scalp oiling or greasing for hair growth or scalp health in a trial. Tier D.
- [Traction alopecia and 'protective' styles](https://vilivity.com/hair/traction-alopecia-and-protective-styles/): Tight braids, weaves and ponytails can cause traction alopecia, hair loss from pulling, and the risk is highest when tension is added to relaxed hair. Tier B moderate.
- [Twist-outs, braid-outs and wash-and-gos: technique](https://vilivity.com/hair/twist-outs-braid-outs-and-wash-and-gos/): No study has tested how to set a twist-out, braid-out or wash-and-go, or how long one lasts. Tier D.
- [Wash day and routine for 4c hair](https://vilivity.com/hair/wash-day-routine-for-4c-hair/): Nobody has tested a wash-day routine for tightly coiled hair. Tier D.
- [Wigs, weaves and lace glue](https://vilivity.com/hair/wigs-weaves-and-hair-glue/): No study has tested whether wigs protect your own hair. Tier D.
- [Winter care and shrinkage for coily hair](https://vilivity.com/hair/hair-in-winter-and-shrinkage/): No study has tested winter care or shrinkage in coily hair. Tier D.

## Mind

- [Anxiety, depression and what helps](https://vilivity.com/mind/anxiety-depression-and-what-helps/): Anxiety and depression are common and treatable, and the NHS says to seek help early. Tier D.
- [Ashwagandha: stress, sleep, thyroid and liver cautions](https://vilivity.com/mind/ashwagandha/): Ashwagandha eased stress and helped sleep a little in short trials, but our search found no trial in Black participants. Tier B moderate.
- [Autism and ADHD: being missed, delayed or misdiagnosed](https://vilivity.com/mind/autism-and-adhd-in-black-children-and-adults/): A US review of 20 studies found delayed diagnosis and misdiagnosis of autism were the main errors, driven by limited knowledge, insurance, provider bias and assessment tools that may not suit Black and Hispanic families. Tier B moderate.
- [Being believed by doctors, and pain](https://vilivity.com/mind/being-believed-by-doctors-and-pain/): Research backs your experience. Tier B moderate.
- [Black men, depression and getting support](https://vilivity.com/mind/mens-mental-health-and-depression/): A survey of African American men found that everyday racism and masculine norms both went with more barriers to seeking help, partly through feeling less in control and more depressed. Tier B thin.
- [Breathwork and slow breathing](https://vilivity.com/mind/breathwork/): Slow breathing practice lowers stress and blood pressure a little in trials of adults generally. Tier B moderate.
- [Childhood trauma and where to start](https://vilivity.com/mind/childhood-trauma-and-where-to-start/): Hard things in childhood, such as abuse, neglect or violence at home, raise the chance of anxiety, depression and PTSD later. Tier B moderate.
- [Colourism, skin tone and mental health](https://vilivity.com/mind/colourism-and-mental-health/): In US surveys of Black adults, experiencing colourism within the community went with higher odds of a psychiatric disorder, and among older adults the link between discrimination and distress was stronger in darker-skinned people. Tier B moderate.
- [Finding a Black therapist or one who understands being Black](https://vilivity.com/mind/finding-a-black-therapist/): Directories in the UK and US list Black or culturally aware therapists. Tier B moderate.
- [Getting a child mental health support](https://vilivity.com/mind/childrens-mental-health-support/): In English child mental health services, children from Black and other minority backgrounds were more often referred through school or social care than through a doctor. Tier B thin.
- [Meditation](https://vilivity.com/mind/meditation/): Meditation is among the better-tested practices here. Tier A moderate.
- [Melatonin for sleep: what it does, dose and rules by country](https://vilivity.com/mind/melatonin-for-sleep/): Melatonin may help you fall asleep a little faster for some people, but reviews disagree, and it did not clearly help adults with long-term insomnia. Tier B thin.
- [Psychosis, sectioning and misdiagnosis in the UK](https://vilivity.com/mind/mental-health-act-psychosis-and-misdiagnosis/): In England, Black people are detained under the Mental Health Act more often than any other group, and a large review found Black Caribbean and Black African patients were far more likely to be compulsorily admitted. Tier B moderate.
- [Racism, racial stress and mental health](https://vilivity.com/mind/racism-and-mental-health/): Many studies find that people who report experiencing racism have worse mental health, including more depression, anxiety and stress. Tier B moderate.
- [Sleep, short sleep and sleep apnoea](https://vilivity.com/mind/sleep-and-sleep-apnoea/): In a US study Black adults were more likely to sleep under six hours and to have sleep apnoea than white adults, and most people with apnoea had never been told. Tier B moderate.
- [Stigma, talking to family and starting therapy](https://vilivity.com/mind/stigma-and-starting-therapy/): A London study found stigma, silence and beliefs about causes slow help-seeking in African-descended communities, including in church groups. Tier B thin.
- [Stress, burnout and blood pressure](https://vilivity.com/mind/stress-burnout-and-blood-pressure/): Reported discrimination is linked to a higher chance of high blood pressure, but the link is small and not proven to be cause. Tier B thin.

## Body

- [A low white cell count that may be Duffy-null (neutrophil count)](https://vilivity.com/body/low-white-cell-count-duffy-null/): Many people of African ancestry are Duffy-null, an inherited blood-cell variant that gives a lower neutrophil count (the white cells that fight infection). Tier B moderate.
- [Alpha-thalassaemia trait: small red cells that are not low iron](https://vilivity.com/body/alpha-thalassaemia-trait-and-low-iron-that-is-not-low-iron/): Alpha-thalassaemia trait means you carry one or two missing copies of the genes that make part of haemoglobin. Tier B moderate.
- [Bowel (colon) cancer screening](https://vilivity.com/body/bowel-and-colon-cancer-screening/): In England the NHS posts a home stool test every 2 years from 50 to 74; US guidance starts at 45. Tier B moderate.
- [Breast cancer, triple-negative disease and screening](https://vilivity.com/body/breast-cancer-and-cancer-screening/): In England, Black women did not have a higher breast cancer rate than White women, but short-term survival was worse in national data, and one London hospital saw younger, more aggressive cases. Tier B moderate.
- [Creatine supplements: strength, kidneys and your kidney test](https://vilivity.com/body/creatine-supplements/): Creatine helps strength gains when you train with weights, in trials of mostly young men, and reviews found no kidney harm in healthy adults. Tier B moderate.
- [Fibroids: symptoms, treatment and pregnancy](https://vilivity.com/body/fibroids-symptoms-treatment-and-pregnancy/): Fibroids are non-cancerous growths in or around the womb, and by 50 more than eight in ten Black women in one US study had them. Tier B moderate.
- [G6PD deficiency: who carries it and what to avoid](https://vilivity.com/body/g6pd-deficiency-what-to-avoid-and-who-carries-it/): G6PD deficiency is an inherited enzyme shortage, common in people with African, Mediterranean and Asian ancestry. Tier B moderate.
- [Glaucoma and eye tests](https://vilivity.com/body/glaucoma-and-eye-tests/): Glaucoma is more common in Black populations at every age, and often has no symptoms until sight is lost. Tier B moderate.
- [Haemoglobin and white cell ranges on your blood test](https://vilivity.com/body/haemoglobin-and-white-cell-reference-ranges/): Blood test ranges were mostly built from white populations. Tier B moderate.
- [Heat, sweating and hydration](https://vilivity.com/body/heat-and-hydration/): I found no study that shows Black people tolerate heat better or sweat differently. Tier D.
- [High blood pressure in Black adults](https://vilivity.com/body/high-blood-pressure-in-black-adults/): The line for high blood pressure is the same for every adult. Tier B moderate.
- [HIV prevention, testing and PrEP](https://vilivity.com/body/hiv-prevention-testing-and-prep/): PrEP is a medicine you take before a possible exposure to HIV, and it is highly effective when taken as prescribed. Tier A strong.
- [How some medicines work differently by gene](https://vilivity.com/body/how-some-medicines-work-differently-by-gene/): Genes change how fast your body breaks down some medicines. Tier B moderate.
- [Ice baths and cold exposure](https://vilivity.com/body/ice-baths-and-cold-exposure/): Ice baths eased muscle soreness after exercise in small, low-quality trials that did not report ethnicity. Tier B moderate.
- [Iron, heavy periods and fibroids](https://vilivity.com/body/iron-and-fibroids/): Fibroids are very common in Black women and start earlier than in White women. Tier B moderate.
- [Kidney disease, the APOL1 gene and the eGFR race adjustment](https://vilivity.com/body/kidney-disease-apol1-and-egfr/): Two variants of the APOL1 gene, common on African chromosomes, raise the risk of some kidney diseases in African Americans. Tier B moderate.
- [Lactose intolerance and dairy](https://vilivity.com/body/lactose-intolerance-and-dairy/): Not every Black person is lactose intolerant, and there is no race rule. Tier B thin.
- [Lung function tests and race correction in spirometry](https://vilivity.com/body/lung-function-tests-and-race-correction-in-spirometry/): A spirometry test measures how much air you can blow out in one breath. Tier B moderate.
- [Lupus: symptoms, risk and getting diagnosed early](https://vilivity.com/body/lupus-in-black-women/): Lupus is a long-term autoimmune condition that causes joint pain, rashes and deep tiredness. Tier B moderate.
- [Magnesium supplements for sleep and cramps](https://vilivity.com/body/magnesium-supplements-for-sleep-and-cramps/): Magnesium tablets did not clearly prevent leg cramps in older adults, and for sleep three small, low-quality trials in older adults hint at falling asleep a little faster. Tier B thin.
- [PCOS, endometriosis and heavy periods](https://vilivity.com/body/pcos-endometriosis-and-heavy-periods/): Heavy or painful periods are not something you have to accept. Tier B thin.
- [Pregnancy risk and safe maternity care for Black women](https://vilivity.com/body/pregnancy-and-maternity-care/): In England, Black women are nearly three times as likely to die during pregnancy or within six weeks of it as White women, in the latest national report. Tier B moderate.
- [Prostate cancer risk and PSA testing](https://vilivity.com/body/prostate-cancer-and-psa-testing/): In England, about one in four Black men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in their lifetime, against about one in eight White men. Tier B moderate.
- [Pulse oximeters and dark skin](https://vilivity.com/body/pulse-oximeters-and-dark-skin/): Pulse oximeters shine light through the skin, and melanin changes how that light behaves. Tier B moderate.
- [Sarcoidosis: symptoms, risk and follow-up](https://vilivity.com/body/sarcoidosis-in-black-adults/): Sarcoidosis is a rare condition where small patches of swollen tissue form, most often in the lungs, skin and lymph nodes. Tier B thin.
- [Sauna and heat bathing: heart health, recovery and risks](https://vilivity.com/body/sauna-and-heat-bathing/): Frequent sauna use went with fewer heart deaths in Finnish men, a link that falls short of proof, and Black participants were tested only in one tiny heat study. Tier B thin.
- [Sickle cell disease, trait and pregnancy](https://vilivity.com/body/sickle-cell-disease-trait-and-pregnancy/): Sickle cell disease is a lifelong inherited blood condition; trait means you carry one copy of the gene and do not have the disease and cannot develop it. Tier D.
- [Sickle cell trait and hard exercise](https://vilivity.com/body/sickle-cell-trait-and-hard-exercise/): Sickle cell trait is one copy of the sickle gene, not sickle cell disease. Tier B moderate.
- [Starting training, rest days and recovery](https://vilivity.com/body/starting-training-rest-days-and-recovery/): Nothing I found says Black adults need a different programme or rest days, so the NHS targets apply: strength work on two days, plus moderate or vigorous activity most days. Tier D.
- [Stroke: signs to act on and what raises the risk](https://vilivity.com/body/stroke-signs-and-risk/): A stroke is an emergency: a drooping face, a weak arm, slurred speech, then call emergency services at once, even if it passes. Tier B moderate.
- [Type 2 diabetes risk and blood sugar](https://vilivity.com/body/type-2-diabetes-risk/): In south London, people with Black African or Black Caribbean backgrounds had two to three times the risk of type 2 diabetes of White British people, and the gap was only partly explained by weight, blood pressure or deprivation. Tier B moderate.
- [Vitamin D and dark skin](https://vilivity.com/body/vitamin-d-and-dark-skin/): Total vitamin D in the blood is lower in Black Americans, but so is the protein that carries it, and one study found the usable amount similar. Tier A moderate.
- [Weight, BMI and losing weight safely](https://vilivity.com/body/weight-bmi-and-ethnicity/): The NHS says people from Black African or African-Caribbean backgrounds are at risk of health problems at a slightly lower BMI: 23 to 27.4 is overweight and 27.5 or more is obese. Tier D.

## Food

- [Apple cider vinegar: weight, blood sugar and safety](https://vilivity.com/food/apple-cider-vinegar/): Apple cider vinegar may lower blood sugar and weight slightly in short trials, but the trials are small and varied, and one well-known weight trial was retracted. Tier B thin.
- [Baobab fruit: blood sugar, iron and vitamin C](https://vilivity.com/food/baobab-fruit/): Baobab fruit is a traditional African food and a source of vitamin C. Tier B thin.
- [Black seed oil (Nigella sativa)](https://vilivity.com/food/black-seed-oil-nigella-sativa/): A 2025 review of 82 studies of black seed (Nigella sativa) found small improvements in blood pressure, blood sugar, cholesterol and body fat, and called it a promising add-on. Tier B moderate.
- [Bovine colostrum supplements for immunity and gut health](https://vilivity.com/food/bovine-colostrum-supplements/): Bovine colostrum, the first milk from cows, has small, mixed trials in athletes and a few other groups, with little effect on immune markers. Tier B thin.
- [Bush teas and herbal remedies (cerasee, bitter leaf) with medicines](https://vilivity.com/food/bush-teas-cerasee-bitter-leaf-and-medicines/): Natural does not mean safe with medicine. Tier B thin.
- [Caribbean and West African diets and health](https://vilivity.com/food/caribbean-and-west-african-diet-and-health/): No trial has tested a traditional Caribbean or West African diet for blood pressure or diabetes, so nobody can say whether it is better or worse. Tier D.
- [Cod liver oil: vitamin D, vitamin A and colds](https://vilivity.com/food/cod-liver-oil/): Cod liver oil is a source of vitamin D, which the UK's NHS says people with dark skin should consider taking all year. Tier B moderate.
- [Does diet cause acne? Sugar, dairy and foods linked to spots](https://vilivity.com/food/diet-and-acne-on-dark-skin/): No diet is proven to treat acne, and the British Association of Dermatologists says a healthy, balanced diet is all it advises. Tier B thin.
- [Fasting in Ramadan with diabetes or sickle cell](https://vilivity.com/food/ramadan-and-religious-fasting-with-diabetes-or-sickle-cell/): With diabetes, fasting in Ramadan can cause low blood sugar and dehydration, and the evidence on sickle cell disease is small and mixed. Tier B thin.
- [Fibroids, food and supplements](https://vilivity.com/food/fibroids-and-diet/): No food has been shown to shrink fibroids. Tier B thin.
- [Hibiscus (sorrel, zobo, bissap) and blood pressure](https://vilivity.com/food/hibiscus-sorrel-blood-pressure/): Hibiscus tea lowered blood pressure a little in several trials, including one in Nigerian adults. Tier A thin.
- [Intermittent fasting for weight and health](https://vilivity.com/food/intermittent-fasting-for-weight-and-health/): Intermittent fasting lost weight in trials, about the same as ordinary calorie cutting, and one small pilot of Black adults in churches found it workable. Tier B moderate.
- [Kola nut: caffeine, the heart and health claims](https://vilivity.com/food/kola-nut/): Kola nut is a traditional stimulant chewed and shared across West Africa. Tier D.
- [Lion's mane and reishi mushroom supplements](https://vilivity.com/food/lions-mane-and-reishi-mushroom-supplements/): Lion's mane and reishi have only small trials behind them, mostly low quality, in older Japanese adults with memory loss, healthy adults, and cancer patients on treatment. Tier B thin.
- [Moringa: blood sugar, blood pressure and general health](https://vilivity.com/food/moringa-leaf-and-blood-sugar/): Moringa leaf is a nutritious food, but a 2025 review of nine trials found no consistent benefit for blood sugar, weight or cholesterol, and rated the evidence very low certainty. Tier B thin.
- [Plantain, yam and cassava: blood sugar and safety](https://vilivity.com/food/plantain-yam-and-cassava-and-blood-sugar/): In glucose tests, cassava, pounded yam and several West African staples raised blood sugar quickly, while breadfruit, white yam, eddoes and tannia were in the middle. Tier B thin.
- [Probiotics and gut health](https://vilivity.com/food/probiotics-and-gut-health/): Probiotics reduced diarrhoea caused by antibiotics in trials, and the UK's NHS says they may ease some IBS symptoms, but evidence for most other claims is thin. Tier B moderate.
- [Salt and blood pressure](https://vilivity.com/food/salt-and-blood-pressure/): Cutting salt lowers blood pressure in Black and non-Black adults alike, and the DASH eating pattern did too in a large US feeding trial that was mostly Black. Tier A moderate.
- [Sea moss (Irish moss): health claims, iodine and heavy metals](https://vilivity.com/food/sea-moss-irish-moss/): My search found no human study showing sea moss improves health. Tier D.
- [Soursop (graviola): cancer cure, blood sugar and safety](https://vilivity.com/food/soursop-graviola/): There is no proof that soursop treats cancer; human studies are lacking. Tier D.
- [Turmeric and curcumin supplements](https://vilivity.com/food/turmeric-and-curcumin-supplements/): Turmeric and curcumin supplements may ease joint pain a little in low-quality trials, but NCCIH says we do not know enough to say they help. Tier B moderate.
- [Vitamins and supplements: what the NHS says](https://vilivity.com/food/vitamins-and-supplements-basics/): The NHS says most people get all the nutrients they need from a varied, balanced diet. Tier D.

## Generational practices

Practices handed down in families, documented by surveys, ethnography or studies. Most are untested and some are harmful. Tier is the evidence for the claim people make; harm is flagged on each.
Machine-readable practices: https://vilivity.com/api/practices/index.json
Hub: https://vilivity.com/practices/

- [African black soap](https://vilivity.com/practices/african-black-soap/): Wash the face and body, and sometimes hair, with a soft soap made from plantain-skin and cocoa-pod ash with palm oil and shea; known as dudu osun or ose dudu. Tier C thin. Harm: possible. Regions: West Africa.
- [Aloe vera (sinkle bible)](https://vilivity.com/practices/aloe-vera-sinkle-bible/): Cut a leaf and use the gel on burns, skin and scalp, or drink it for "sugar"; in rural Somalia aloe gel is also put in the eye. Tier B thin. Harm: possible. Regions: Caribbean, East and Southern Africa.
- [Ash, cow dung or heat on the baby's umbilical cord](https://vilivity.com/practices/umbilical-cord-ash-cow-dung-and-hot-compress/): Birth attendants and relatives cut the cord with a razor blade and dress the stump with ash, cow dung or a hot compress. Tier B moderate. Harm: yes. Regions: West Africa.
- [Being strong and hiding distress](https://vilivity.com/practices/the-strong-black-woman-and-hiding-distress/): Carry on, keep distress private, and avoid asking for help; a cultural legacy of strength. Tier B thin. Harm: possible. Regions: Black British, African American.
- [Bitter leaf (Vernonia amygdalina)](https://vilivity.com/practices/bitter-leaf/): Wash the leaves to remove bitterness and cook them in soup, or squeeze and drink the bitter juice, for malaria, "sugar" and stomach complaints. Tier B thin. Harm: possible. Regions: West Africa.
- [Bush medicine taken alongside diabetes and blood pressure tablets](https://vilivity.com/practices/bush-medicine-alongside-diabetes-and-blood-pressure-drugs/): Take bush teas or herbal remedies for "sugar" and "pressure" in addition to, or sometimes instead of, prescribed medicines; about a third of Barbadian church-goers use herbal remedies. Tier C thin. Harm: possible. Regions: Caribbean.
- [Bush tea for a "washout" or "blood cleanse"](https://vilivity.com/practices/bush-tea-washout-and-blood-cleanse/): Drink a bitter or purgative bush tea (cerasee and others), often as a regular tonic or at the turn of the year, to "wash out" or "clean the blood". Tier C thin. Harm: possible. Regions: Caribbean.
- [Cerasee (bitter melon) tea](https://vilivity.com/practices/cerasee-tea-bitter-melon/): Boil the vine leaves of cerasee (Momordica charantia) and drink the bitter tea, for "sugar" (diabetes), colds, skin and as a cleansing tonic. Tier B thin. Harm: possible. Regions: Caribbean.
- [Chebe powder](https://vilivity.com/practices/chebe-powder/): Mix roasted chebe seed powder with oil or fat and coat the lengths (not scalp) before plaiting, repeating every few days. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: West Africa, Central Africa.
- [Chemical relaxers, often started in childhood](https://vilivity.com/practices/chemical-relaxers-from-childhood/): Use a lye or no-lye relaxer to straighten the hair every few weeks to months, often starting as a girl. Tier B moderate. Harm: yes. Regions: African American, East and Southern Africa, West Africa, Black British.
- [Cooking with shea butter](https://vilivity.com/practices/shea-butter-as-cooking-fat/): Use shea butter as a cooking fat in northern Ghana and the savanna belt of West Africa. Tier B thin. Harm: none. Regions: West Africa.
- [Eating clay (geophagy) and ice (pagophagia) in pregnancy](https://vilivity.com/practices/clay-eating-geophagy/): Some women, especially in the rural South, eat white or red clay, and some pregnant women eat large amounts of ice or freezer frost. Tier B moderate. Harm: yes. Regions: African American.
- [Eating patterns of Somali families in the UK](https://vilivity.com/practices/somali-diet-in-the-uk/): Eat mainly rice, pasta and red meat with little fruit or vegetable; cultural beliefs about food shape the diet. Tier D. Harm: low. Regions: Black British, East and Southern Africa.
- [Fever grass (lemongrass) tea for fever](https://vilivity.com/practices/fever-grass-lemongrass-tea/): Drink fever grass (Cymbopogon citratus) tea to bring down a fever, often for children, with a shared home tradition of "sweating it out". Tier D. Harm: low. Regions: Caribbean.
- [Food taboos in pregnancy](https://vilivity.com/practices/dietary-taboos-in-pregnancy/): Pregnant women avoid certain foods because of family rules and beliefs about the baby and about witchcraft. Tier B thin. Harm: possible. Regions: East and Southern Africa.
- [Garlic and ginger for high blood pressure](https://vilivity.com/practices/garlic-and-ginger-for-blood-pressure/): People with hypertension take raw garlic or ginger, in food or water, alongside or instead of tablets. Tier B thin. Harm: possible. Regions: West Africa.
- [Greasing the scalp (and pressing with a hot comb)](https://vilivity.com/practices/greasing-the-scalp-and-hot-combing/): Part the hair and rub a grease, pomade or oil onto the scalp, often as a weekly routine before braiding or pressing. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: African American, Caribbean, Black British.
- [Hair threading (irun kiko)](https://vilivity.com/practices/threading-irun-kiko/): Wrap sections of hair in black or coloured thread from root to tip to stretch and style it, often for girls and women. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: West Africa, Central Africa.
- [Herbal concoctions in pregnancy and to start labour](https://vilivity.com/practices/herbal-concoctions-in-pregnancy-and-to-start-labour/): Women drink herbal mixtures through pregnancy, to induce labour or to boost health, often from family or friends, and often without telling the clinic. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: West Africa, East and Southern Africa.
- [Herbal teas, ginger, lime and spices for colds and flu](https://vilivity.com/practices/herbal-teas-and-spices-for-colds-and-flu/): Drink hot infusions, decoctions and "punch" made from local herbs (mint family especially), often with ginger, lime or honey, at the first sign of a cold; Haitian families did this in the COVID period. Tier D. Harm: low. Regions: Caribbean.
- [Hot compress on the abdomen after birth](https://vilivity.com/practices/postpartum-hot-compress-on-the-abdomen/): After delivery a mother presses hot cloths or hot water bottles to the lower abdomen, often daily for weeks. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: West Africa.
- [Hot salt-water sitz bath after birth](https://vilivity.com/practices/postpartum-hot-sitz-bath/): Sit in a bowl or bath of hot water (sometimes with salt) in the first days and weeks after delivery. Tier D. Harm: low. Regions: West Africa.
- [Hot water fomentation of the baby's soft spot](https://vilivity.com/practices/hot-fomentation-of-newborn-fontanelle/): Press hot cloths or heated water to a newborn's fontanelle (and body) to "mould" the head or soothe the baby. Tier B thin. Harm: yes. Regions: West Africa.
- [Hot water, hot food and pepper soup after birth](https://vilivity.com/practices/postpartum-hot-water-hot-food-and-pepper/): For weeks after birth the mother drinks hot water, eats hot (temperature) and very peppery food and bathes in hot water. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: West Africa.
- [Isihlambezo, umhlabelo and imbiza in pregnancy and infancy](https://vilivity.com/practices/zulu-isihlambezo-umhlabelo-and-imbiza/): Zulu women take isihlambezo during pregnancy, umhlabelo for postpartum recovery and imbiza for babies. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: East and Southern Africa.
- [Jamaican black castor oil on the scalp and edges](https://vilivity.com/practices/jamaican-black-castor-oil-on-scalp-and-edges/): Massage black castor oil into the scalp and hairline for growth, thickness and edges. Tier C thin. Harm: low. Regions: Caribbean, African American, Black British.
- [Kola nut](https://vilivity.com/practices/kola-nut-chewing/): Chew kola nut for alertness and stamina, offer it in hospitality and ritual, and (in one Nigerian custom) rub a kola paste on a pregnant belly. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: West Africa.
- [Oiling and massaging newborns](https://vilivity.com/practices/newborn-oil-massage-and-petroleum-jelly/): Rub cooking oil, other natural oils or petroleum jelly into a newborn after bathing; massage the belly with a kola paste in some Nigerian communities. Tier B thin. Harm: low. Regions: West Africa, East and Southern Africa.
- [Orthodox Christian fasting](https://vilivity.com/practices/ethiopian-orthodox-fasting/): Observe the Orthodox fasts (no animal products on many days, including Wednesdays, Fridays and long seasons such as the Assumption fast). Tier B thin. Harm: possible. Regions: East and Southern Africa.
- [Palm wine, alcohol and tea to bring in milk](https://vilivity.com/practices/postpartum-lactation-drinks-palm-wine-and-tea/): Mothers drink tea, hot water, palm wine or other alcoholic drinks to "improve the flow" of breast milk. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: West Africa.
- [Planning exercise around your hair](https://vilivity.com/practices/planning-exercise-around-hair/): Change hairstyle for exercise or skip workouts to protect a style that took hours and money. Tier B thin. Harm: low. Regions: African American.
- [Plants for childbirth recovery and vaginal "cleansing" (Haitian and Caribbean women)](https://vilivity.com/practices/haitian-and-caribbean-plants-for-childbirth-and-vaginal-cleansing/): Women use food plants as teas, baths and vaginal preparations after childbirth and for gynaecological infections or "cleansing"; the practice continues after migration. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: Caribbean.
- [Prayer and the church as mental health support](https://vilivity.com/practices/prayer-and-faith-as-coping/): Turn to prayer, scripture, the pastor or the congregation when distressed, instead of or before therapy. Tier B thin. Harm: low. Regions: African American, Caribbean, Black British.
- [Prayer camps, faith and traditional healers for mental illness](https://vilivity.com/practices/traditional-and-faith-healing-for-mental-illness/): Families take people with psychosis or severe distress to a traditional healer, prayer camp or church; some centres use shackling, flogging and forced fasting. Tier D. Harm: yes. Regions: West Africa, East and Southern Africa.
- [Putting mascara, kohl, aloe, honey or breast milk in babies' eyes](https://vilivity.com/practices/traditional-eye-remedies-for-babies-and-children/): Apply mascara-type eye cosmetics to a newborn's eyes, or instil aloe, honey, plant sap or breast milk for red or sore eyes. Tier B thin. Harm: yes. Regions: West Africa, East and Southern Africa.
- [Root work and Gullah herbal remedies](https://vilivity.com/practices/root-work-and-gullah-herbal-remedies/): Families in the South and Sea Islands use teas, poultices and spiritual practice drawn from herbal lore; the tradition is documented in books. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: African American.
- [Satin bonnet, scarf or pillowcase at night](https://vilivity.com/practices/satin-bonnet-and-scarf-at-night/): Cover the hair with a satin or silk bonnet or scarf, or sleep on a satin pillowcase. Tier D. Harm: none. Regions: African American, Caribbean, Black British, West Africa.
- [Skin lightening and bleaching creams](https://vilivity.com/practices/skin-lightening-and-bleaching/): Apply lightening creams, soaps or injections (hydroquinone, steroids, sometimes mercury) to the face or whole body, often for years, often from a young age. Tier B moderate. Harm: yes. Regions: West Africa, Caribbean, African American, Black British.
- [Sorrel (hibiscus) drink](https://vilivity.com/practices/sorrel-drink/): Steep dried sorrel calyces (Hibiscus sabdariffa) with ginger and cloves, sweeten and chill; a Christmas staple in Jamaica and drunk through the year; known as zobo or sobolo in West Africa. Tier B moderate. Harm: low. Regions: Caribbean, West Africa.
- [Soursop leaf tea](https://vilivity.com/practices/soursop-leaf-tea/): Steep soursop (graviola) leaves, or eat or juice the fruit, for sleep, nerves, "sugar", and increasingly as a cancer remedy. Tier C thin. Harm: yes. Regions: Caribbean.
- [Tight braids, weaves and extensions on relaxed hair](https://vilivity.com/practices/braids-and-extensions-on-relaxed-hair/): Put in tight cornrows, braids or extensions as a protective, low-maintenance style for weeks at a time. Tier B moderate. Harm: yes. Regions: West Africa, East and Southern Africa, African American, Black British.
- [Traditional birth attendants' herbal remedies](https://vilivity.com/practices/traditional-birth-attendant-herbs/): Traditional birth attendants give herbal remedies for threatened miscarriage, labour complications, retained placenta and postpartum bleeding. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: East and Southern Africa.
- [Treating "high blood" by how you feel](https://vilivity.com/practices/high-blood-and-high-pertension/): Older Black women describe "high blood" or "high-pertension" as something felt in the blood and nerves, and manage medication by those symptoms. Tier B thin. Harm: possible. Regions: African American.
- [Tying cloth tightly around the abdomen after birth](https://vilivity.com/practices/postpartum-abdominal-binding/): Tie a wrapper or cloth tight across the belly after delivery, for days or weeks. Tier B thin. Harm: possible. Regions: West Africa.
- [Vaginal steaming and herbal feminine cleansing](https://vilivity.com/practices/vaginal-steaming-and-feminine-cleansing/): Sit over herbal steam or use herbal washes to "clean" the womb after periods or birth; promoted through wellness networks. Tier D. Harm: possible. Regions: African American, West Africa, Caribbean.
- [Vicks VapoRub on the chest, feet and nose](https://vilivity.com/practices/vicks-vaporub-on-chest-and-feet/): Rub Vicks on the chest, back, soles of the feet (under socks) or under the nose for colds, coughs and asthma, including on children. Tier B moderate. Harm: possible. Regions: Caribbean, African American, Black British, West Africa.
- [Washing hair every few weeks](https://vilivity.com/practices/infrequent-hair-washing-and-long-gaps-between-wash-days/): Keep a style in for weeks and wash only now and then, often once every two to four weeks, longer in braids or weaves. Tier B thin. Harm: low. Regions: Black British, African American.
- [Wearing hair natural in later life](https://vilivity.com/practices/natural-hairstyles-and-wellbeing-in-older-black-women/): Stop relaxing and wearing complex styles; wear the natural texture. Tier B thin. Harm: none. Regions: Black British.

### Reported but not yet documented

- [Cocoa butter on stretch marks](https://vilivity.com/practices/cocoa-butter-on-stretch-marks/): reported, no opened source shows people do it. Tier A moderate. Harm: none.
- [Epsom salt baths](https://vilivity.com/practices/epsom-salt-baths/): reported, no opened source shows people do it. Tier C thin. Harm: low.
- [Irish moss (sea moss) drink](https://vilivity.com/practices/irish-sea-moss-drink/): reported, no opened source shows people do it. Tier D. Harm: possible.
- [Moringa](https://vilivity.com/practices/moringa-for-health-and-milk/): reported, no opened source shows people do it. Tier B moderate. Harm: low.
- [Shea butter on skin, hair and babies](https://vilivity.com/practices/shea-butter-on-skin-hair-and-babies/): reported, no opened source shows people do it. Tier B thin. Harm: low.
